standard_prerequisites.name: Sign and triviality criteria for invertible sheaves on a proper curve
standard_prerequisites.use: Turns a nonzero section vanishing at a point into strict positivity of the degree.

standard_prerequisites.name: The Riemann-Roch type formula for the Euler characteristic of powers
standard_prerequisites.use: Gives chi(X, L^n) = n deg(L) + chi(X, O_X), which drives the growth estimate.

core_obligations: Forward direction: from ampleness obtain a power L^{tensor n} with a section s whose nonvanishing locus is affine, use that X is not affine to see that s vanishes somewhere, and conclude deg(L^{tensor n}) > 0, hence deg(L) > 0 by multiplicativity (proof lines 10005-10013).
Converse, growth: use that dim_k H^0(X, L^{tensor n}) is at least chi(X, L^n) = n deg(L) + chi(X, O_X), which grows linearly in n when deg(L) > 0 (proof lines 10016-10021).

Converse, separation: deduce from the growth that sufficiently high powers admit sections separating any prescribed finite set of closed points, and conclude by the ampleness criterion (remaining lines up to 10067).
proof_roadmap: Show ampleness forces positive degree via an affine nonvanishing locus and vanishing.
For the converse, estimate the growth of sections of the powers.
Use the growth to separate finitely many points and apply the ampleness criterion.
difficulty_reason: The lemma characterizes ampleness of an invertible sheaf on a proper curve by positivity of its degree. For the forward direction the proof uses that an ample sheaf has a power with a section whose nonvanishing locus is affine, that the curve is not affine, hence the section vanishes somewhere, so the degree of that power is positive, and multiplicativity of the degree gives positivity of the degree of L (proof lines 10005-10013). The converse uses that dim_k H^0(X, L^{tensor n}) is at least chi(X, L^n) = n deg(L) + chi(X, O_X), which grows linearly, so for any finite collection of closed points one can find sections separating them; this yields the ampleness criterion (proof lines 10016 onwards to line 10067). H2: the two directions each combine a degree computation with a section-existence argument, and the growth estimate is the key step of the converse.
